insurer: Niva Bupa Health Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: Base Sum Insured options mentioned: 2L; 3L/4L; 5L/7.5L/10L/15L/25L/40L/45L/65L/70L/90L/95L (Policy Schedule will specify actual SI). Deductible is mandatory as per Policy Schedule.

good.name: Initial waiting period: 30 days (standard)
good.quote: 30-day waiting period (Code- Excl03): a. Expenses related to the treatment of any Illness within 30 days from the first Policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an Accident, provided the same are covered.
good.explanation: Non-accident illnesses are not covered in the first 30 days; accidents are covered from day 1.

good.name: PED waiting period: 36 months (good as per rules)
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a Pre-existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first Policy.
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are covered after 36 months of continuous coverage (3 years is acceptable as per your benchmarks).

good.name: Specific disease/procedure waiting period: 24 months (standard)
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first Policy with us.
good.explanation: Listed specific conditions (e.g., cataract, hernia, etc.) are covered after 24 months.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization cover: 60 days
good.quote: We will pay above mentioned Pre-hospitalization Medical Expenses only for period up to 60 days immediately preceding the Insured Person’s admission
good.explanation: Covers eligible medical expenses incurred up to 60 days before hospitalization (reimbursement basis).

good.name: Post-hospitalization cover: 90 days
good.quote: We will pay Post-hospitalization Medical Expenses only for up to 90 days immediately following the Insured Person’s discharge
good.explanation: Covers eligible medical expenses up to 90 days after discharge (reimbursement basis).

good.name: Domiciliary hospitalization covered
good.quote: We will indemnify on Reimbursement basis only, the Medical Expenses incurred for the Insured Person’s Domiciliary Hospitalization during the Policy Period
good.explanation: Home treatment can be covered when medically necessary and meets conditions (e.g., at least 3 consecutive days and inability to move/bed unavailability).

good.name: NCB/Renewal bonus (Cumulative Bonus) available: 5% per year up to 50% (resets not mentioned in the provided text)
good.quote: We will provide Loyalty Additions in the form of Cumulative Bonus by increasing the Sum Insured applicable under the Policy by 5% of the Base Sum Insured of the immediately preceding Policy Year subject to a maximum of 50% of the Base Sum Insured.
good.explanation: Sum Insured can grow on renewal (5% per year up to 50%) subject to conditions (e.g., applicable only for Base SI up to ₹25 lakh). The wording shared does not explicitly state whether it resets on claim—confirm from schedule/insurer.

bad.name: Room rent has a % cap (can trigger proportionate deductions)
bad.quote: Room Rent (per day) Up to 1% of Base Sum Insured per day
bad.reference: Annexure I (Product Benefit Table) – Room Rent (per day)
bad.explanation: A room rent cap can restrict room choice and may lead to reduced claim settlement if a higher room is chosen.

bad.name: Proportionate deduction applicable if higher room category is used
bad.quote: If the Insured Person is admitted in a Hospital room where the room category opted or Room Rent incurred is higher than the eligibility as specified in the Policy Schedule, then We shall be liable to pay only a pro-rated portion of the total Associated Medical Expenses... (Eligible Room Rent limit / Room Rent actually incurred) * total Associated Medical Expenses
bad.explanation: If you choose a room above eligibility, the insurer can proportionately reduce associated expenses (doctor fees, OT, nursing etc.), increasing out-of-pocket cost.

bad.name: No restore benefit: Sum Insured is NOT replenished after a claim
bad.quote: Thereafter only the balance Sum Insured after payment of claim amounts admitted shall be available for future claims arising in that Policy Year.
bad.explanation: This wording indicates the Sum Insured reduces with claims and only the remaining balance is available; no restore/recharge of SI is described in the provided text.

bad.name: Consumables not covered (Annexure III lists many common consumables as not payable/subsumed)
bad.quote:
ANNEXURE III  The expenses that are not covered or subsumed into room charges / procedure charges / costs of treatment
List  I – Expenses not covered
... 56 GLOVES ... 60 MASK ... 57 NEBULISATION KIT ... 58 ANY KIT WITH NO DETAILS MENTIONED [DELIVERY KIT, ORTHOKIT, RECOVERY KIT, ETC]
bad.reference: Annexure III (List I – Expenses not covered; also Lists II–IV)
bad.explanation: Many common hospital consumables/items may be non-payable or forced to be included under package heads; this can increase out-of-pocket expenses depending on hospital billing.

bad.name: Modern treatments have sub-limits (not at actuals up to SI)
bad.quote: The following procedures / treatments shall be covered only up to the sub-limit as specified for each procedure / treatment in the below table: ... Robotic surgeries 2.5 Lac ... Stereotactic radio surgeries 3.5 Lac ...
bad.explanation: Even if your Sum Insured is high, payouts for listed modern procedures are capped at defined amounts.

bad.name: Mandatory annual aggregate deductible (super top-up style structure)
bad.quote: You have to mandatorily choose an annual aggregate claim Deductible amount, options of these Deductible amounts are provided in the section ‘Product Benefit Table’.
bad.explanation: This is a deductible-based plan: the insurer starts paying only after you first pay claims up to the chosen deductible in a policy year. This can significantly increase out-of-pocket for smaller/medium claims.

bad.name: Ambulance benefit has a low cap
bad.quote: Emergency Ambulance Up to Rs.1,500 per hospitalization
bad.reference: Annexure I (Product Benefit Table) – Emergency Ambulance
bad.explanation: ₹1,500 per hospitalization is typically insufficient in many cities, leading to extra out-of-pocket.

bad.name: Mental illness sub-limit for some conditions (disease sub-limit)
bad.quote: The following disorders / conditions shall be covered only up to 10% of Base Sum Insured or Rs. 50,000, whichever is lower.
bad.explanation: For listed mental health conditions (e.g., severe depression, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder), payouts are capped, which can restrict coverage if treatment costs are higher.

unclear.name: Co-pay terms not explicitly stated (verify policy schedule / product benefit table for any co-payment option)
unclear.quote: The following claim cost sharing options shall apply under the Policy if specified in the Policy Schedule and shall apply to all Insured Persons.
unclear.explanation: The document defines co-payment but does not clearly state a default co-pay % (if any). Confirm from Policy Schedule whether any co-payment applies.

unclear.name: NCB/Loyalty Additions: whether it resets on claim is not stated in the shared wording
unclear.quote: We will provide Loyalty Additions in the form of Cumulative Bonus by increasing the Sum Insured... by 5%... subject to a maximum of 50%...
unclear.explanation: The bonus accrual is clear, but the text provided does not specify what happens to accumulated bonus after a claim (whether it reduces/resets). Confirm from schedule/insurer.
